title: With Due Respect (Vol. 7) -- Ch. 6: Healing of the Heart
keywords: the three lower courts of medicine
your coronary arteries are all clear
primary_topics: Chapter 6 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7) -- CJP's April 12, 2009 Easter Sunday Inquirer column, 'a story of faith' recounting his 1996 heart scare and what he believes was a miraculous healing

The cascade of cardiac tests in 1996 under Dr. Dante Morales -- ECG, treadmill, 2-d echo and finally an angiogram -- memorably likened to appealing a case from the trial courts up to the Supreme Court
The healing Mass said by Fr. Pascual Adorable for an ailing colleague (Justice Ricardo Francisco), during which CJP prayed only for Francisco and was himself 'prayed over'

The 'stunning' result -- 'your coronary arteries are all clear' -- which CJP, 'as a believer,' attributes to divine intervention, closing on the conviction that 'for man it may not be possible but for God nothing is impossible'
sub_topics: The Easter frame: on the day Christians 'commemorate the resurrection,' CJP offers 'a story of faith,' noting Easter 'is glorious for it celebrates [the Lord's] conquest of death, sin, and human frailties'

The check-up: in March 1996, accompanying his wife Leni to cardiologist Dr. Dante Morales, he consulted about 'dizzy spells, cold sweat, and chest pains'; an ECG led to a treadmill test that came back 'positive for myocardial ischemia,' suggesting thick heart muscle or blocked arteries

The regimen: Morales told him to 'avoid fat and salt, stop... tennis, slow down on golf,' keep his heartbeat below 100, and prescribed aspirin, Betaloc, Zocor, Lexotan and nitroglycerin -- pending a third test, the 2-d echo

The 'courts of medicine': after the 2-d echo, Morales advised an angiogram, quipping that 'the ECG is equivalent to the Municipal Trial Court; the treadmill to the Regional Trial Court; the 2-d echo, to the Court of Appeals; and the angiogram, to the Supreme Court' -- 'since we lost in the three lower courts of medicine, we should appeal to the highest court'

Second opinions and a friend's help: with the angiogram postponed to April 13, CJP's friend Pat Garcia arranged a consult with his cousin, US-based heart surgeon Dr. Jorge Garcia, who suspected 'coronary ischemia' in the rear of the heart

The healing Mass: his colleague Justice Ricardo Francisco -- himself ailing in heart and kidneys -- asked Fr. Pascual Adorable to say a private 'Healing Mass' on March 22, during which CJP 'prayed ardently for Justice Francisco' and 'totally forgot about [his] scheduled angiogram,' before Fr. Adorable 'prayed over' each justice and spouse, including Leni and him

The result: anticipating possible bypass surgery, he entered Makati Medical Center reading the Yale 'Heart Book'; during the angiogram on April 13, as the dye spread, 'Dr. Morales exclaimed, "Your coronary arteries are all clear!"' -- a 'complete clearance' he had not expected -- later confirmed by Dr. Garcia: 'when you die, it will not be due to any heart problem'

The conviction: medical 'buffs' and 'agnostics' may explain it otherwise, but 'as a believer,' CJP holds that 'the praying over and the healing Mass made all the difference,' that the Lord 'completely cured' him (still 'robust' 13 years later), and -- having prayed only for Francisco -- that 'the Lord remembered' and 'knew [his] needs more than [he] did,' one of several life-miracles proving 'for man it may not be possible but for God nothing is impossible'

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 6 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7), CJP's April 12, 2009 Easter Sunday Inquirer column, is 'a story of faith' about his 1996 heart scare and what he believes was a miraculous healing. Accompanying his wife Leni to cardiologist Dr. Dante Morales that March, he consulted about 'dizzy spells, cold sweat, and chest pains'; an ECG and a treadmill test came back 'positive for myocardial ischemia,' and Morales -- after a 2-d echo -- advised an angiogram, quipping that the tests were like courts: 'the ECG... the Municipal Trial Court; the treadmill... the Regional Trial Court; the 2-d echo... the Court of Appeals; and the angiogram... the Supreme Court,' so 'since we lost in the three lower courts of medicine, we should appeal to the highest.' With the angiogram postponed, his friend Pat Garcia arranged a second opinion from US-based surgeon Dr. Jorge Garcia, who suspected coronary ischemia. Meanwhile his ailing colleague Justice Ricardo Francisco asked Fr. Pascual Adorable to say a private 'Healing Mass' on March 22, during which CJP 'prayed ardently for Justice Francisco' and forgot his own looming procedure, before Fr. Adorable 'prayed over' each justice and spouse. Anticipating bypass surgery, he entered Makati Medical Center reading the Yale 'Heart Book' -- but during the April 13 angiogram, as the dye spread, 'Dr. Morales exclaimed, "Your coronary arteries are all clear!"', a complete clearance later confirmed by Dr. Garcia ('when you die, it will not be due to any heart problem'). Medical 'buffs' and 'agnostics' might call it coincidence, but 'as a believer' CJP holds that 'the praying over and the healing Mass made all the difference' -- and that, having prayed only for Francisco, 'the Lord remembered' him too, proof that 'for man it may not be possible but for God nothing is impossible.'
